headline: Medium risk: dbt-core can write to warehouses while langchain4j can mediate LLM-driven actions, creating default-path data leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, dbt-core can call a data warehouse and langchain4j is an LLM integration library; if outputs are manually bridged or copied into prompts, attacker-controlled warehouse content could influence downstream instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies dbt-generated text or warehouse content into a langchain4j prompt
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not paste dbt output into prompts without sanitizing
Add a provenance banner to any copied text
requires-engineering: add content filtering before prompt ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, while langchain4j is an LLM framework that may send prompts to external model APIs depending on configuration. Even though langchain4j shows no explicit egress here, the pair can still move warehouse data into model prompts in default integration patterns, creating a sensitive-data leakage path.
conditions: IF warehouse rows or dbt artifacts are forwarded into langchain4j prompts
IF langchain4j is configured to use a remote model provider
mitigations: Restrict prompts to redacted samples
Disable remote model providers for sensitive runs
Review dbt artifacts before forwarding them
Use a separate non-sensitive staging dataset
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on prompt construction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and warehouse API access, while langchain4j shows no write or network capability in the profile. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource or shared lock domain, so write-write conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because the profiles are sparse, so the lower severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same warehouse objects
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking
mitigations: Keep write scopes disjoint
Assign separate service accounts
Avoid shared mutable directories
requires-engineering: add optimistic-locking or lease coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce transformed warehouse outputs, and langchain4j can consume those outputs as model context or tool input. If langchain4j treats dbt output as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinated interpretations can cascade into downstream actions or user-facing responses. The interaction is plausible in default integration patterns, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF langchain4j uses dbt output as prompt context or tool arguments
IF no verification step checks dbt-produced facts before use
mitigations: Insert a validation step before reuse
Require source links for any derived claim
Limit langchain4j to summarization, not action-taking
Flag low-confidence dbt outputs explicitly
requires-engineering: add schema and semantic checks

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core is documented as touching data warehouse data, but no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is shown. langchain4j has no data classes touched and no compliance metadata here, so a concrete compliance breach is not established. Because the profiles are incomplete, the safest supported finding is a low-severity gap rather than none.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records and langchain4j forwards them to a non-compliant model provider
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the warehouse and the model backend
mitigations: Classify the warehouse dataset before use
Block regulated fields from prompts
Confirm provider residency and retention settings
Document deletion/export handling
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement at prompt assembly
